catholic-encyclopedia-1913-angelo-secchi: A 1913 entry on Angelo Secchi — the Jesuit father of astrophysics. Joseph Pohle honors his star spectra. His classes mapped the heavens' chemistry. The Roman College housed his telescopes. A priest among the astronomers. His moon craters bear his name. His observatory crowned the Roman College.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-magli: This 1913 reference piece on Antonio Magliabechi — the Florentine prince of bibliophiles. Klemens Löffler honors his vast library. His books founded the national collection. Scholars pilgrimaged to his door. The miser who hoarded books. His correspondence fills the archives. His bequest opened to every reader.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ausonio-franc: This 1913 reference piece on Ausonio Franchi — the Italian philosopher. Charles Dubray weighs his restless system. He left the priesthood for the schools. The Church answered his errors. A thinker beyond the fold. His Ultima Critica stated his creed. His break grieved his old friends.
